prompt:
Use case: historical-scene / production modeling reference.
Create one large high-resolution model reference sheet with exactly FIVE separate orthographic views of the SAME German Panzerkampfwagen II Ausf. F light tank, front, rear, left side, right side, and straight top view. A serious realistic asset reference, never toy, blocks, stylized cartoon. Arrange five spacious clean panels on pale warm gray with thin dividers, accurate consistent scale within front/rear pair and side pair. Label panels FRONT, REAR, LEFT, RIGHT, TOP. Panzer II F has a compact low angular welded hull, five equally spaced medium rubber-rim road wheels on EACH side, four small return rollers above each side, front drive sprockets and rear idler wheels, narrow continuous individual steel track shoes with grousers. Small offset angular polygonal turret on the left-forward roof, modest 20mm slender cannon and smaller coaxial barrel, small commander cupola at turret rear, rectangular driver visor on forward left casemate, right engine deck grilles, rear exhaust with perforated heat shield, mudguards, tow hooks, tools. Target bounding dimensions approx hull 4.81m long, overall 2.28m wide, turret roof/cupola 2.15m high. Turret points straight forward in all views. Apply consistent dark neutral panzer-gray painted steel, subtle paint wear and dust, exposed graphite metal tracks, nearly black rubber tires, restrained physically plausible roughness; no dramatic damage or battle. All views show same tank and same accessories. Orthographic projection only, no perspective, no three-quarter view, no shadows obscuring geometry, no people, terrain, national insignia or slogans. This is a visual reconstruction reference, not an engineering blueprint; no dimension annotation or fake exact measurement scale.
layout: one reference board with five named view panels
modeling: The coding assistant inspected the generated board, authored a bounded scene/preset, and operated the Jarvis plugin. Jarvis has not automatically reconstructed geometry from pixels.
accuracy: Approximate visual study, not OEM dimensions or scan.
